text: I saw a therapist at the university counselling service who did CBT with me, which helped with the panic attacks, especially learning that panic can't actually hurt me. My GP put me on sertraline for about a year, which took the edge off. Grounding exercises (5 things you can see etc) help with the DR. What didn't help: friends telling me to 'just relax' or that it was 'only a bad trip'. I still get some DR when I'm very tired.
Mit Freunden darüber geredet, ansonsten hat die Zeit geholfen.

I've tried a lot of things. First I contacted the retreat center, who told me I needed to come back and drink again to integrate the experience. I didn't. That felt very harmful and I've since learned other people had similar experiences there.

I found an integration therapist through a psychedelic harm reduction organisation. That was the first thing that helped a bit, mostly because she didn't think I was crazy and she knew others who had been through similar things. We did weekly sessions for about a year.

I also saw a psychiatrist who put me on an SSRI (escitalopram), which helped the depression a little, and quetiapine for sleep, which helped me sleep but made me feel even more like a zombie. I stopped the quetiapine after a few months.

Meditation made things much worse at first. Every time I closed my eyes and focused inward I felt like I was slipping back into the void. A teacher at a meditation center told me to 'sit with it' and I had a panic attack in the middle of the session. Later, with my therapist, I tried very gentle body-based practices with eyes open, which were OK.

Exercise helped, especially running, because it made me feel my body. Being in nature during the day also helped.

Honestly the biggest factor has been time. It's been almost three years and I'm much better, but I'm not the same as before and I'm still struggling with the existential side of it.
Nothing, it went away on its own

Ich war beim Augenarzt und beim Neurologen, beide haben nichts gefunden. Der Neurologe hat mir Lamotrigin verschrieben, das hat das Visual Snow etwas abgeschwächt. Am meisten hilft mir, es nicht ständig zu beobachten und es zu akzeptieren. In Foren über HPPD zu lesen hat mir am Anfang eher Angst gemacht.
I read a lot about other people's DMT experiences online, which helped me feel less alone. I talked to the friend I did it with. Meditation helped me calm the fear of death a bit.

I worked with an integration coach recommended by the retreat for a few months, which was somewhat helpful but expensive. Then I found a psychotherapist who specialised in anxiety and she really helped me understand the panic and stop being afraid of the DR itself. I started yoga and long walks, and cut out caffeine and alcohol completely for a year. Time was definitely a factor. What wasn't helpful was going to my GP, who didn't take it seriously and said 'well, that's what happens with drugs'.

Ich habe eine Therapie angefangen, aber nach ein paar Sitzungen abgebrochen, weil ich mich nicht verstanden gefühlt habe. Am meisten haben mir Gespräche mit meiner Partnerin geholfen. Das Misstrauen ist aber nicht ganz weg.
Didn't need to do anything about it.

In the beginning it was mainly the psychiatric treatment: antipsychotics (risperidone, later switched to aripiprazole because of side effects), and regular appointments with a psychiatrist. That stopped the psychosis but didn't help the depression or the fear much. After about six months I started seeing a psychologist for CBT, which was very helpful for the fear of relapse. She helped me learn to notice the 'meaning-making' thoughts without panicking and to test them against reality. I tapered off the antipsychotics after a year with my psychiatrist's support.

My family was a huge help. They didn't judge me and they made sure I got out of bed every day. My mum walked with me every morning.

I joined an online support group for HPPD, which was mixed. Some people were very helpful, others were very negative and made me more scared.

Exercise and a regular sleep schedule made a big difference. I stopped using all substances, including alcohol and caffeine, for two years.

Things that were harmful: one doctor at the hospital who told me I had probably 'unlocked' schizophrenia and would need medication for life. That terrified me for months and turned out not to be true. Also reading internet forums at night.

Ich habe eine Psychotherapie gemacht, die mir sehr geholfen hat, die Erfahrung einzuordnen. Außerdem habe ich angefangen zu meditieren und viel über Philosophie und Existenzialismus gelesen. Gespräche mit Freunden, die ähnliche Erfahrungen gemacht hatten, waren auch hilfreich.
